unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
Gregor, Sep 2025: In May 2025, the total cost of developing Phase 1 was announced as US $6.878 billion. For now, I've split this cost equally between Phase 1.1 and Phase 1.2 (US $3.439 billion each), even though we don't really how this will get split up or what final cost will be.

As of Q3 2025, three distinct phases of the Argentina LNG project are  taking shape: 
• Phase 1 (5.95 mtpa) to be developed by YPF, Golar, Pan American Energy and others)
• Phase 2 (10 mtpa) to be developed by YPF and Shell (Shell has replaced Petronas, who dropped out of the project in 2024)
• Phase 3 (12 mtpa) to be developed by YPF and Eni

Only two of these phases are currently mentioned on YPF's official Argentina LNG website: https://argentina-lng.ypf.com/. 
However, recent quarterly reports from YPF (Q1 and Q2 2025) clearly include the Golar project as part of Argentina GNL: 
• https://inversores.ypf.com/r/documents.html?p=Informacion-financiera/YPF%20-%20ER%20-%201T25%20-%20ESP.pdf
• https://inversores.ypf.com/r/documents.html?p=Informacion-financiera/YPF%20-%20ER%20-%202Q25%20-%20ESP%20v1.pdf

YPF appears to have abandoned its plans for an onshore terminal in favor of a three-phase offshore project comprising six FLNG units (two FLNGs per phase):
https://buenosairesherald.com/business/energy/ypf-to-build-six-lng-boats-in-rio-negro-instead-of-onshore-plant

GEM previously identified the YPF/Golar phase as a separate project under the name Golfo San Matias FLNG. However, after consulting with Rob and Amalia, I am now merging both parts of the YPF/Golar phase into the Argentina LNG project under the names Phase 1.1 and Phase 1.2, and I'm deleting the original database record under the old name Golfo San Matias FLNG.

Note that GIIGNL has offered conflicting descriptions of the relationship between Argentina GNL and the Golfo San Matias FLNG project. This first GIIGNL reference -- https://www.giignl.org/news/argentinas-ypf-joins-pae-and-golar-to-develop-flng-project -- clearly identifies them as separate projects, while this other one -- https://www.giignl.org/news/eni-ypf-seal-argentina-lng-deal -- identifies Golar FLNG Hilli as Phase 1 of the Argentina GNL project, with the Shell/YPF deal called Phase 2 and the Eni/YPF deal called Phase 3. 

AL: This is the Hilli Episeyo FLNG. 

AL: I'm having trouble figuring out if both vessels will be located at the same location; there's still not enough info available for MK II as of June 2025 to tell, but it's good to check again in the future. The location I added was based on the Environmental Impact Statement for the project that addressed only the Hilli FLNG. Both vessels are being treated as one project, sometimes referred to as the Southern Energy project - Argentina GNL 1. https://www.harbourenergy.com/news-and-media/latest-news/2025/southern-energy-sa-final-investment-decision/

GC, Dec 2024: New export terminal announced in july 2024, to be developed by Southern Energy S.A., a JV between Pampa Energía, Harbour Energy, Golar LNG and others, with anticipated FID in 2025 and start-up in 2027.

GC, Aug 2024: Location has been moved from Bahía Blanca to Sierra Grande in Río Negro state. Projected capacity has increased to 30 mtpa, to be constructed in three stages, with initial commissioning of first FLNG unit as early as 2027 and full commissioning estimated for 2032; Gregor, July 2023: The companies developing this project have not yet state a specific start year, but in 2022 they said the project could take a decade to complete, so we’re estimating 2032 loosely for now. We expect a more precise start date within the next year, assuming this project moves forward as planned. https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/argentinas-ypf-petronas-talks-over-gas-pipeline-lng-plant-source-says-2022-09-01/?utm_source=Inside+Gas&utm_campaign=80d542d896-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2022_09_08_09_40&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_5666c2a85c-80d542d896-208473805Gregor

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit: AL, Jun 2025: terminal is still idled; Argentina is only importing LNG from Escobar terminal. GC, Sep 2024: GIIGNL's 2024 report shows no vessel docked here, and I can't find any other source that documents LNG import activity here in 2024, so I've switched status from Operating to Idle. Gregor, Jul 2023: Nice report on LNG in Argentina: https://www.oxfordenergy.org/wpcms/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/Unconventional-Gas-in-Argentina-Will-it-become-a-Game-Changer-NG-113.pdf
unit_rows.ResearcherNotesProject: AL Jun 2025: The terminal was operational between 2008 and 2018 and then between 2021 and 2023. FSRU history: The first was the regasification vessel Excelsior, which fulfilled its task for four seasons, from June 2008 to the end of 2011, to be later replaced by the Express and at the end of 2015. It was later succeeded by the Exemplar, the same vessel that in 2018 Mauricio Macri fired to start a failed export process with the barge Tango and then returned in 2021 and 2022. In 2023, the Excelsior returned and the terminal has been idled since 2024. Gregor has added teh Excellence FSRU (2011 - wiki). https://argenports.com/nota/un-invierno-sin-buque-regasificador-en-bahia-blanca-y-con-la-mira-en-exportar/

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit: AL, 2025: Terminal will probably continue to be inactive/serve as import terminal (Bahía Blanca GasPort). GC, Sep 2024: Terminal is still inactive, and likely to remain so, given the ongoing development of three larger export terminal projects in Argentina (Argentina GNL, Golar-Pan American and TGS Puerto Galván).
unit_rows.ResearcherNotesProject: AL 2025: At the time terminal was operational (2019-2020), vessel (Tango FLNG) was owned and operated by Exmar. It has since changed owner/operator (Eni) and is now in Republic of Congo.

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
AL Jun 2025: I'm having some doubts regarding the wording of the capacity statements; what I'm thinking is that the total production will be between 4 and 5.4 mtpa, and each train will contribute equally to that, but they're still undecided about the exact final capacity. The project is also going to be built in 2 stages, with the first having 2 trains, with a capacity to produce between 2 and 2.5 mtpa. I'm changing it to 5.4 mtpa in the database but leaving Gregor's notes, wiki info, and sources, since I also feel this remains rather speculative. There haven't been any new updates since July 2024, however. https://www.parlamentario.com/2024/07/03/tgs-remarco-su-intencion-de-operar-gnl-en-bahia-blanca/ 
GC, Sep 2024: This project would consist of up to 4 trains, each with a capacity of 4 million cubic meters per day. Since this all remains rather speculative, I'm treating it as a single project with a capacity of 16 million cubic meters per day (5.84 bcm/y). We can break it down into phases later if it actually moves forward.
